SMTO-GML-0074 — Gmail turned the connection away before sign-in finished

GUID: c4eb56a2-8b4b-5206-8b54-5211e9a70a52
Slug: gmail-imap-session-rejected
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-imap

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open your Gmail mailbox, but Gmail refused the connection before sign-in completed. This doesn't prove your app password is wrong, and no mail was touched in this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a conversation, ask SMTO to test the Gmail connection, and type @ to pick the same Gmail account the request used. The connection test signs in without changing any mail and shows whether Gmail keeps refusing this account.
  2. Sign in to Gmail in a web browser with the same address and look for a security alert from Google. If Google asks whether the sign-in was you, confirm it. Google can block mailbox connections from other apps until you confirm them.
  3. If the Gmail address belongs to a work or school, ask its Google administrator whether email apps and app passwords are allowed for your account. An administrator setting can make Gmail refuse the connection even when the password is right.
  4. If the test still fails, create a new app password in your Google Account, then open More options › Parameter Store, select the Gmail account, and replace the app password in its Value tab. A deleted or replaced app password is one common reason Gmail refuses to sign in.

What success looks like

  • The Gmail connection test succeeds, and your original Gmail request finishes with a result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch to a different Gmail account or sign-in method to get around this, and if an earlier request was sending or changing mail, check Gmail before asking for it again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's IMAP session to imap.gmail.com:993 received an IMAP4.error (greeting or LOGIN rejection) before authentication completed, so no mailbox session was established.

What this means

  • IMAP setup or login returned a protocol rejection before an authenticated session was established. Existing execution and mutation uncertainty remain authoritative; response prose cannot supply a missing cause.

Why this can happen

  • IMAP4.error occurs before box.authenticated, potentially during greeting or login.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Run gmail.test_connection for the same account_ref and read the error_kind in the Gateway result; any IMAP4.error raised before box.authenticated maps here and the provider text is deliberately omitted. Check Google security alerts, Workspace IMAP and app-password policy, and concurrent connection limits; replace app_password in the gmail_app_password_account parameter only after a credential rejection is confirmed.
  • Test the account connection and inspect the recorded connection stage and IMAP access policy. Check credentials only if a login rejection is independently established.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
